title: SLO breach: tiered circuit-breaker + cross-region routing interaction (root cause + remediation tracker)
creator: Olivia Park
summary: On 2026-02-26 we observed a sustained SLO breach for tail latency in production caused by an unintended amplification between the region-level circuit-breaker hysteresis and cross-region failover routing. Automatic failback created oscillations and overloaded secondary regions, triggering load-shedding that increased client-visible errors. This doc records timeline, root cause, immediate mitigations, and concrete remediation actions with owners and due dates.
description: Incident surfaced as an increase in 99th percentile generation latency and a spike in 5xx errors for multi-region customers. The control plane had recently rolled out a hysteresis change to the regional circuit-breaker thresholds (ENG-47012) intended to reduce false negatives; coincidentally a routing policy change (ENG-47890) that preferred nearest-region with fast failback was deployed the same week. Under a gradual traffic surge from a marketing campaign, backpressure caused primary-region breakers to open briefly, routing switched to secondaries, then the hysteresis timing allowed rapid re-closure which immediately routed traffic back. This oscillation caused token bursts and KV cache thrashing on secondaries, exceeding capacity and triggering load-shedding rules. The result: SLO misses for 3 hours and visible errors for ~7% of requests in affected tenants.
timeline: 2026-02-26 02:08Z - First alert: 99p latency exceeded SLO on primary region A (observability: console/runtime dashboard)
2026-02-26 02:12Z - Circuit-breaker on region A tripped to Open for 12s due to queued request spike
2026-02-26 02:12Z - Smart routing moved ~18% traffic to region B and C as fallback
2026-02-26 02:14Z - Circuit-breaker hysteresis closed on A (recent change decreased min-open time), traffic shifted back
2026-02-26 02:15Z - Oscillation detected: A -> B -> A within 90s; KV cache warmups on B produced high memory & GPU IO
2026-02-26 02:20Z - Load-shedding policy engaged on region B (rejects at queuing layer), client 5xx increased
2026-02-26 02:45Z - On-call mitigations: throttled routing to region B and disabled aggressive failback policy
2026-02-26 04:00Z - Latency normalized after conservative routing enforced and manual backpressure adjustments
2026-02-26 05:30Z - Incident declared resolved; follow-up meetings scheduled
root_cause: Interplay of two independent changes: (1) reduced circuit-breaker minimum open/hysteresis window that allowed rapid reopen/close cycles, and (2) a routing failback policy that prioritized immediate return-to-primary. Under surge these combined to cause rapid fanout and cache churn on secondary regions. Operationally, there was no protective pairing between routing policies and circuit-breaker configuration, and monitoring did not surface oscillation fingerprints quickly enough.
impact_metrics: SLO breach duration: 3 hours (primary latency > 99p target)
Customer error rate: 5xx increased from baseline 0.3% to 7.2% for affected tenants
Affected requests: estimated 1.2M requests routed through oscillating path
Tail latency: p99 increased from 180ms to 1.9s during peak
action_items: Ravi Menon - Adjust circuit-breaker hysteresis defaults to enforce a 30s min-open window for region-level breakers by 2026-03-05 (blocker for oscillation)
Maya Li - Introduce routing-policy coupling: routing controller must respect active breaker state and avoid immediate failback for 60s after a breaker event by 2026-03-07
Alexandre Dupont - Add an oscillation detector signal to Console SLO dashboards (new metric: region-flap-rate) and set alert at >3 flaps/5m by 2026-03-10
SRE rotation - Create runbook entry: "When cross-region failover is observed, temporarily pin fallback traffic and escalate to platform on-call" (owner: Platform SRE team) complete by 2026-03-03
Performance - Implement KV cache warmup smoothing on secondaries to limit simultaneous cache fill IO (owner: Serving Runtime) target 2026-04-01
Product - Update rollout checklist to require cross-team sign-off on any change to routing or breaker behavior (owner: PM-Liv) by 2026-03-12
Observability - Add a composite alarm that fires when (breaker-open-rate > threshold) AND (routing-shift > 10%) to reduce detection time (owner: Monitoring team) due 2026-03-08
On-call training - Run a 1-hour postmortem tabletop for platform & SRE engineers covering this failure mode (owner: Olivia Park) scheduled 2026-03-16
followups: Design a canary plan for hysteresis changes that exercises simulated traffic surges before global rollout
Perform chaos test that simulates simultaneous partial-region thrash with failback enabled (include KV cache metrics), track results in ENG-49001
Audit all routing and circuit-breaker parameter changes in last 6 months and flag overlapping deployments
Re-run SLO sensitivity analysis with the new hysteresis defaults to quantify cost-latency tradeoff
links: Related tickets: ENG-47012 (breaker hysteresis change), ENG-47890 (routing failback policy)
notes: Trade-offs considered: increasing min-open time protects against oscillation but can extend failover time during legitimate region outages — settled on 30s min-open as pragmatic balance
Decision log: we chose routing-policy coupling to avoid future unintended interactions rather than only hardening breaker settings
Stakeholder feedback: Sales and Customer Success flagged 4 enterprise customers impacted; Compensation offers will be coordinated by CS once engineering sign-off on cause is complete
Retrospective: need better pre-deploy coordination and an automated gating test for combined routing+breaker changes
